item.title: Kentucky rushes for season-low in disappointing loss to Florida
item.description: Kentucky hosted the Florida Gators as its final night game of the 2026 season at Kroger Field. It was a weird, back-and-forth game in which Florida left with a win. The game was full of storylines, with transfers on both sides, but primarily involving the coaches on the Gators’ sideline. Jon Sumrall, former player and coach at Kentucky, would return to his old Kentucky home for the first time since his departure in 2022 to be the head coach at Troy. Another coach over on that sideline was Kentucky’s defensive coordinator under Mark Stoops for the final six years of his tenure in Lexington. No doubt those two would want to go back to Gainesville with a win, with both having a chip on their shoulder heading into the contest. Well, the two defensive-minded coaches got to leave with smiles on their faces after a 21-14 victory for Florida. How did they do it? Well, they stopped the run. Kentucky came into the night averaging 163.7 yards on the ground per game, and left tonight’s contest with only 61 yards. Start to finish, the Florida defense never let Kentucky get rolling at all. The offense tried everything they could to get something going, from throwing different players out there to different formations and motions, but nothing helped. Florida came in with a plan to stop Kentucky on the ground, and they executed it. CJ Baxter, Jason Patterson, Jovantae Barnes, Mikkel Skinner, Brennen Ward, and Kenny Minchey all had their chances to run the ball, and none could break through. In all honesty, Minchey may have looked the best, even though he only ended the game with one yard due to sack yards. “Didn’t establish the run tonight, at all,” Stein said about the struggling run game. “Got out-physicalled at the point of attack. That, to me, was the early indication: not being able to run the ball; you run it for 61 yards on 27 carries. And they rush it for 211 on 48; that’s a problem. We’ve gotta address it and get it fixed.” Kentucky won’t have a chance at the dream season we had all started to believe in with them dropping out of the College Football Playoff, but there’s still pride to play for, as Stein and multiple players said. Running the ball for over 100 fewer yards will help you end the season with four straight losses if you’re not careful. With a road game to Missouri on deck and a home game against Louisville following it, Kentucky’s offense has got to figure some things out in the run game. It was unacceptable against Florida and is certainly one of the more eye-opening stats when you look at how Kentucky defeated Florida.

item.description: Camilo Duran – “Both his legs cramped, but he’s fine,” Colombia boss eases Celtic concerns Camilo Duran’s injury scale in Colombia’s 1-0 friendly victory over Chile in Cali, thankfully has turned out to be no more than the Celtic striker suffering from cramp… Camilo Duran of Celtic celebrates scoring his team’s third goal with Benjamin Nygren of Celtic and Callum Osmand of Celtic during the UEFA Europa League match between Celtic FC and Besiktas JK at Celtic Park on November 05, 2026. item.title: Newark Catholic graduate Wright coaches Otterbein to OAC record
item.description: WESTERVILLE - The Otterbein volleyball team stands above the rest in the history of the Ohio Athletic Conference. Otterbein swept visiting Muskingum, 25-22, 25-10, 25-17, on Nov. 14 to win an OAC-record fifth consecutive tournament championship. The Cardinals have been coached throughout their run by Newark Catholic graduate Monica (McDonald) Wright. "Otterbein has been very good to me, and we have had tons of great girls come through the program," said Wright, who has led the Cardinals for two dominant decades shortly after starring as a player at Wittenberg. "We are in an awesome spot where we have six seniors still with the program. When you have that much experience on the floor and the tradition here - I am just super proud of them." Watkins Memorial graduate Elise Adelman piled up 32 assists and added eight kills and nine digs for Otterbein in the championship match. Adelman has played for the Cardinals the past two seasons after setting multiple program records during two seasons at Bloomsburg. "This team is something special. We've had a great season, and we are not done yet. We knew we had to battle, and we did just that," Adelman said. "As soon as I came here, something in me changed. This program, it's a family. I am so happy to be here." Lexi Scott, a Zane Trace graduate, led a a balanced attack with 12 kills to take tournament Most Outstanding Player honors. She, Adelman and Emerson Baum represented Otterbein on the all-tournament team. NC graduate Sydney Gummer totaled four kills and two assisted blocks. Gummer, who has had a standout freshman season after helping the Green Wave win the Division VI state championship a year ago, led the Muskies with 16 kills in their semifinal victory against Mount Union. Sheridan graduate Alexis Bradley, the Muskies’ setter, joined teammate Mackenzie Krous on the all-tournament team. Otterbein this week will continue their impressive season in the NCAA tournament. The Cardinals have qualified for the postseason for the 12th time in 19 seasons under Wright. "(Wright) expects the best from me every day," Adelman said. "She pushes me every day. She knows I can only get better." ksnyder@newarkadvocate.com 740-973-4541 Instagram: @newarkurt This article originally appeared on Newark Advocate: Newark Catholic graduate Wright coaches Otterbein to OAC record

item.title: ’Simply to get a…’- NFL’s latest Drake London fine sparks blunt response from J.J. Watt
item.description: Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images J.J. Watt has questioned the NFL after Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London was handed another hefty fine for unnecessary roughness, with the former defensive end suggesting the league may be trying to provoke a reaction. London was fined $23,882 for using his helmet against Cincinnati Bengals cornerback DJ Turner II during the Falcons’ Week 9 game in Madrid. The latest punishment comes after London was already fined $12,537 for an incident involving Tampa Bay Buccaneers linebacker Alex Anzalone. Both violations were first-time offences in their respective categories. J.J. Watt questions NFL’s decision to fine Drake London again Watt did not hold back when reacting to the latest punishment on X, resharing NFL insider Tom Pelissero’s report. “They have to be doing this simply to get a reaction out of people sometimes… It worked. Twenty. Three. Thousand. Dollars. For this?” Watt posted. The incident occurred with seconds remaining in the third quarter against Cincinnati. After making a 21-yard reception, London lowered his head as he collided with Turner, resulting in the unnecessary roughness penalty. The two fines have now made for an expensive stretch for the Falcons receiver. According to the NFL’s rules, another helmet-related unnecessary roughness violation would see his fine increase to $47,762. London is also tied for the largest fine handed out in Week 9, alongside Seattle Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones, who received the same $23,882 punishment. It has been a difficult campaign for the 24-year-old, who has recorded 44 catches for 692 receiving yards and one touchdown. Atlanta have also struggled, sitting at 3-6 despite London signing a contract extension that keeps him with the franchise through the 2030 season. His disciplinary issues have extended beyond the two fines, too. Earlier in the campaign, London was involved in an exchange with a fan during the Carolina Panthers game, admitting afterwards that he needed to take responsibility for his response. “I’m going to be honest here, I don’t take light to disrespect at all,” London said. “I don’t care who you are. I’m a man, too, at the end of the day. So, if you want to get on a personal level, I can get there, too, but it’s not the right thing to do. So, I got to take accountability for that, and I got to push forward and be the bigger man in some of those situations.” The NFL distributes fine money equally between NFLPA retired player support programmes, the NFL Foundation and other non-profit organisations supporting youth sports, community health and player safety. item.title: How many points A’ja Wilson needs in 2027 to break into WNBA all-time top-10 scoring list
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Since being drafted as the first overall pick by the Las Vegas Aces in 2018, A’ja Wilson has cemented herself as one of the greatest players in the league’s history. The Aces came up short in the WNBA playoffs in 2026 but it was still a fantastic personal campaign for Wilson. She ended the regular season with the highest average across the league (26.2) ahead of Kelsey Mitchell (24.7) and Caitlin Clark (22.3). A’ja was similarly impressive in the postseason (27.5 average) and was also named the WNBA MVP for a record fifth time earlier this year. Now, while the 2027 campaign won’t begin for a while, she is almost certainly going to cement her name in the history books during it. As per Basketball Reference , the Aces star currently has 6,792 total career points in the WNBA. That puts her 11th in the all-time scoring list. However, she could break into the top 10 after just one game, as Wilson is only 11 points behind the now-retired Sue Bird, who occupies 10th place with 6,803 points. As well as Bird, A’ja could surpass 9th-place Cappie Pondexter (6,811) but may face a more difficult task when it comes to overtaking 8th. That position is held by Breanna Stewart (6,860), who is still active and will be competing with Wilson in the coming season. Meanwhile, though A’ja is a prolific points scorer, she is still some way off ever reaching the WNBA’s all-time points scorer, Diana Taurasi (10,646). item.title: From World Cup Heartbreak to a Netherlands Double for Arsenal’s Jurriën Timber
item.description: From World Cup Heartbreak to a Netherlands Double for Arsenal’s Jurriën Timber Jurriën Timber scored his first two senior international goals on Friday night as the Netherlands thrashed Greece 7-0 in the Nations League. It was a memorable night in Amsterdam for the Arsenal defender, who had to watch the World Cup from afar this summer after injury forced him out of the Dutch squad. Timber Scores Either Side of Half-Time OnsOranje reports that Timber started at left-back for Xavi Hernández’s side. Crysencio Summerville opened the scoring and Tijjani Reijnders hit a first-half hat-trick before Timber turned in Donyell Malen’s delivery from close range to make it 5-0 in the 40th minute. Timber was in the right place again just before the hour, arriving at the post to score his second. Malen added the seventh, while Timber’s Arsenal teammate Christos Tzolis started on the opposite side for Greece. The win leaves the Netherlands top of their Nations League group ahead of Monday’s trip to Germany. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) From World Cup Heartbreak to Goals for Club and Country Five months ago, Timber had been named in the Netherlands’ World Cup squad only for a fresh injury setback to rule him out of the tournament . He described himself as heartbroken at missing the chance to represent his country on that stage. Timber returned to action for Arsenal this season, but in October he spoke about why he was taking care not to rush his comeback . He wanted to play every game and take part in every training session, but knew he had to listen to the physios as he rebuilt his fitness. Later that month he opened the scoring in Arsenal’s 3–0 Champions League win over Lille , after Noni Madueke urged him to shoot. His goals against Greece came from much closer in, but both showed how dangerous he can be when he follows an attack into the box. For Arsenal fans, seeing Timber back and starting for his country was already good news. Seeing him score twice, after what he went through in the summer, made it an even better night. Gooners, did Arsenal miss Timber more for what he gives us at the back or for what he adds going forward? Let’s hope he returns to Arsenal duty with his scoring boots on! item.title: Wolff sees F1 history in Hamilton and Verstappen's unforgettable podium moment
item.description: Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff believes the image of Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen lifting Kimi Antonelli onto their shoulders after his maiden Formula 1 championship triumph in Mexico will be remembered for decades. The Italian's title celebrations produced one of the most striking moments of the season, with two of Formula 1's biggest names joining forces to honour the sport's newest world champion. Hamilton and Verstappen, who finished second and third respectively, lifted Antonelli into the air during the podium celebrations , creating an image that Wolff believes perfectly captures the passing of generations in Formula 1. Speaking to the BBC, the Mercedes boss reflected on the significance of the moment and the remarkable circumstances that brought the three drivers together. "I think this is going to be the iconic photo for many decades to come. What an interesting coincidence that they finished second and third and lifted him up. It's almost like three generations of drivers. They come in like every ten years, and they had the potential future champion on their shoulders when he won his first world championship." Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures The photograph carries particular significance given the careers of the three drivers involved. Hamilton, a seven-time world champion, represents an era in which Mercedes established itself as Formula 1's dominant force, while Verstappen subsequently emerged as the sport's leading figure during Red Bull's period of success. Antonelli's arrival at the top of Formula 1 now represents another generational shift, with the Italian achieving the ultimate prize at an early stage of his career. For Wolff, who has overseen Antonelli's development through the Mercedes junior programme, the moment also represents the culmination of years of investment in the young driver's potential. Wolff credits Antonelli's family for his success Beyond the celebrations in Mexico, Wolff also highlighted the influence of Antonelli's family in shaping the character of the newly crowned world champion. The Mercedes team principal believes the Italian's upbringing has played a crucial role in helping him handle the expectations and pressure that accompany a career at the highest level of motorsport. "His parents are really down-to-earth people. Father, racing driver, runs his own teams. They have the right values. They're humble. They're loyal. They're respectful. So, certainly a major part in making Kimi who he is today." Antonelli's father, Marco, has extensive experience in motorsport as both a driver and team owner, providing his son with a close connection to racing from an early age. That background helped Antonelli progress through karting and the junior single-seater categories before securing his opportunity with Mercedes.

item.title: Erling Haaland Breaks Long-Held Silence on Manchester City Guilty Verdict on Norway Duty
item.description: Erling Haaland Breaks Long-Held Silence on Manchester City Guilty Verdict on Norway Duty How did Manchester City fans react to the independent panel guilty verdict on September 29? More Videos Haaland, 26, scored an 88th-minute penalty in Norway's 3-1 UEFA Nations League win over Wales on Saturday night, after Antonio Nusa and Andreas Schjelderup had put the hosts in control in the second half. An independent commission found Manchester City guilty on 114 of 115 charges relating to the nine seasons from 2009-10 to 2017-18, in a verdict published on 29 September that found the club's revenues had been inflated and its costs reduced by more than £900 million. City declared their innocence on the day of the ruling and lodged a comprehensive appeal at 7pm on 1 October, with the hearing reported to be scheduled for mid-December and any sanctions not expected until next year. This is a question I struggle to answer, says Haaland in defiant response to Man City guilty verdict Speaking to TV 2 Sport after the win over Wales, Haaland was asked about the verdict as the Manchester City number nine finally addressed the elephant in the room. The Leeds-born striker said: "It didn't start until 2009-2018, so 2009, I think I played for Bryne FK in 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013. Should we continue? "So this is a question I struggle to answer. It's a legal battle; I don't know how to say it in Norwegian. It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City , which will be brought up with a panel and such. "Should I answer this? item.title: Mike Tomlin still thinks about NFL’s ‘scary’ $100,000 fine that nearly ruined his reputation in 2013
item.description: Photo by Rob Carr/Getty Images NFL legend Mike Tomlin recently recalled an incident from 2013 that still haunts him. Since leaving the Pittsburgh Steelers, NFL icon Mike Tomlin has been vocal about his 25-year career in the league. Keeping that in mind, Tomlin recently shed some light on a 2013 incident that led to the NFL issuing a $100,000 fine to him. Many may have already guessed, but if not, Tomlin talked about the time he almost collided with Baltimore Ravens receiver Jacoby Jones in 2013. Mike Tomlin says the ‘truth’ didn’t save him from the NFL Tomlin recalled the moment during his appearance on the ‘Not Just Football’ podcast, where he claimed that he reflected on being investigated by the NFL despite sharing the truth about the controversial play. “The truth didn’t save me from a fine. I got fined $100,000 after the ball was kicked. I looked up at the jumbotron to watch what was happening. “I see myself come into the jumbotron. That’s when I discovered that he was coming up our sideline,” Tomlin said. He added, “Spatially, I get disoriented where I am, and I’m watching something that I don’t want to happen. … I saw myself on the jumbotron. “And when I saw myself and I saw where I was, I just immediately moved to my left. It was scary, you know what I mean? ‘Cause I thought I was going to get run over.” While Tomlin claims it was unintentional, the NFL still handed him a $100,000 fine for standing too close to the field during Jones’ kickoff run. It has been nearly 13 years since the incident, but Tomlin seemingly still often thinks about how he nearly collided with the Ravens star. item.title: Bayern Munich set price tag of up to €300 million for Real Madrid target – report
item.description: Bayern Munich set price tag of up to €300 million for Real Madrid target – report Before signing Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig for around €140 million, Michael Olise was by far Real Madrid’s most important target in the summer transfer window. The club were in talks with Bayern Munich over prising away the French international, who is now regarded as one of the best players in world football. Florentino Perez was keen on making Olise the next big Galactico signing after Kylian Mbappe. But the move never materialised, as Bayern Munich simply weren’t keen on offloading their star player. Bayern Munich set price tag of up to €300 million Bayern Munich have no desire to sell Olise anytime soon. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) According to Diario AS , it appears Bayern Munich have made the route to sign Olise a lot harder by setting a price tag of up to €300 million. As one of the biggest players in world football, Bayern Munich are more than aware of the fact that Olise’s valuation has soared significantly in the past few years. Having signed him from Crystal Palace for just €53 million in 2024, the German giants are now demanding a whopping €300 million. The Bavarians’ valuation has been further backed by the fact that Olise has a long-term contract at Allianz Arena until 2029 and has shown no desire to force his way out of the club. Bayern Munich, though, have been unable to convince the player to sign a contract extension just yet. When asked about the talks stalling, honorary president Uli Hoeness said, “The time will come to reach a new agreement. He has two more years of contract.” The report does suggest the final decision on his future may ultimately rest with the player himself next summer. Olise’s complex character and Real Madrid’s position Olise has been involved in 19 goals for Bayern Munich in all competitions this season. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) According to the report, there is another factor that clubs are weighing up when it comes to Olise. The winger is known for a somewhat distant and unusual character off the pitch, something that has not gone unnoticed by major clubs across Europe. For Real Madrid, then, any future pursuit of Olise looks astronomically expensive and far from straightforward, given the fact that Bayern Munich have set such a high price tag and have no desire to sell him . With his contract running until 2029, Real Madrid can do nothing but play the waiting game for the time being. The Spanish giants must also first resolve the future of underperforming star Vinicius Jr., whose potential exit could go a long way in freeing up the space required to sign a big player lile Olise.

item.title: Declan Rice Welcomes Alex Scott Competition as Arsenal Weigh Bournemouth Move
item.description: Alex Scott Declan Rice says he is relishing competition from Alex Scott for an England midfield place. Arsenal , Rice’s club, are among the sides linked with a big-money move for the Bournemouth midfielder. Scott, 23, made his England debut in the 2-0 win over the Czech Republic in Prague, before earning his first start four days later. That debut came off the bench on Tuesday 29 September. Thomas Tuchel described Scott as the complete package after his first start, a 7-0 win over Croatia in the Nations League. Scott then picked up an injury. He withdrew from the squad with a quadriceps problem that was first expected to sideline him for six to eight weeks. Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose later said the injury was better than expected. Scott still missed this month’s camp. He was ruled out of Tuchel’s squad for the Croatia and Spain games with a thigh injury. Rice spoke ahead of Sunday night’s Nations League match against world champions Spain in Madrid. It is England’s final group game, and both sides have already reached the quarter-finals. A win would give England top spot in Group A3. “To be honest, Alex Scott playing was incredible,” Rice said per The Mirror . “The way he’s been playing for Bournemouth the last two or three seasons has been remarkable.” “The way he’s being spoken about is totally right because of the levels he’s set for himself and I totally understand playing for England comes with competition.” Rice said he already faces that competition at club level. “When we [Arsenal] signed Bruno Guimaraes, when we signed [Martin] Zubimendi, when we had Myles [Lewis-Skelly], [Mikel] Merino, [Martin] Odegaard, you’re competing with six midfielders at your club every day so for me there’s nothing different.” “Throughout my whole career there’s been competition. It’s normal.” Arsenal have signed a midfielder this year already. They completed the signing of Guimaraes from Newcastle in August for a reported £75m. Their interest in Scott dates back to the summer.Bournemouth rejected Arsenal’s initial approach and said they would not sell him anytime soon. The latest reports came last week. According to The i Paper, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all made exploratory enquiries about Scott. The i Paper reported that Liverpool and Chelsea are keenest on a January move, while Arsenal would prefer to wait until the summer. Bournemouth reportedly value Scott at more than £100m for a January departure. Sources close to Bournemouth dismissed suggestions that an £80m offer could open negotiations. The Telegraph has reported that Bournemouth intend to reject interest in Scott and two other key players in January, as they chase European qualification for a second successive season. Scott’s contract situation adds to the interest. He reportedly has 18 months left on his deal and has turned down two new contract offers.

item.title: Aryna Sabalenka denies claims she directed Russian insult at Ukrainian opponent Elina Svitolina
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka has denied claims that she directed an insult at Ukrainian opponent Elina Svitolina but apologised for her comments after a viral clip showed her swearing during her WTA Finals exit. The World No 2 was caught on camera angrily cursing in Russian during her 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat to Svitolina , with some interpreting the Belarusian’s comments as derogatory towards her opponent or Ukrainians in general. Sabalenka sought to clarify the incident in a statement posted on Instagram on Saturday evening. “My comment was not directed at Elina,” she said. "I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment. "That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended. “Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament.” Svitolina’s triumph over Sabalenka at Indian Wells was her first in seven matches against the 28-year-old. Elina Svitolina got her first win in seven matches against Aryna Sabalenka (Getty) Amid the ongoing war, Ukrainian players do not shake hands with Russian or Belarusian players, nor do they take pre-match photographs with each other. But Svitolina responded to Sabalenka’s statement by calling for their matches to be “respected”. She said: "As we see there's many, many Ukrainians, many, many flags and of course they want me to win this particular match. "We've played many times with Aryna. She has her fans. I have my fans. "I just hope the matches between us [are] respected. Sometimes in some matches that we've played also there have been not great comments towards me in regards of the war. "It is like this in the social media, sometimes the things are turned around a little bit." Svitolina will face Mirra Andreeva in the climax of the WTA Finals after the Russian teenager thrashed Linda Noskova 6-2 6-1 in the semi-finals.

item.title: Tim MacMahon explains what LaMelo Ball is doing to keep Timberwolves relevant even without Anthony Edwards
item.description: Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images LaMelo Ball is making a difference at both ends of the court as the Minnesota Timberwolves continue to win without injured superstar Anthony Edwards, according to ESPN’s Tim MacMahon. Minnesota have put together a five-game winning streak despite Edwards undergoing a knee procedure that is expected to keep him out for two months. Ball has averaged 20.5 points, 3.9 rebounds, 6.3 assists and 1.8 steals across the eight games Edwards has missed. However, it is his defensive improvement that has caught MacMahon’s attention. Tim MacMahon highlights LaMelo Ball’s defensive improvement in Minnesota Timberwolves Speaking about Ball’s performances, MacMahon praised the guard’s work on the defensive end: “LaMelo is playing the best defense of his career,” MacMahon said. “I was going to say his brother Lonzo might tell you he’s playing defense for the first time in his career, but he’s guarding.” “Certainly, you can’t question Melo’s talent. Kuminga is doing what they hoped he would do. Dosunmu, his shooting splits are phenomenal. So they’re still getting elite production from the shooting guard position.” That improvement is reflected in the numbers. Ball currently has a career-best individual defensive rating of 105, compared to his seven-year career average of 114. The Timberwolves have also been considerably stronger defensively with him on the court. They are allowing 101.0 points per 100 possessions when Ball plays, compared to 111.7 when he sits. Minnesota are currently the NBA’s best defensive team, conceding just 103.8 points per 100 possessions. Rudy Gobert, a four-time Defensive Player of the Year, remains central to that success, but Ball’s contribution has given the team another important option. There has also been plenty of support offensively. Jonathan Kuminga is averaging 12.4 points per game, while Jaden McDaniels is producing a career-best 16.9. Ayo Dosunmu has also stepped up with 18 points per game and shooting splits of .522/.469/.897. MacMahon highlighted their contributions, saying: “Certainly, you can’t question Melo’s talent. Kuminga is doing what they hoped he would do. Dosunmu, his shooting splits are phenomenal. So they’re still getting elite production from the shooting guard position.” Hall of Famer Dwyane Wade has also defended Ball against previous criticism, arguing that his reputation does not reflect the player he is. With Edwards expected to miss two months, Minnesota will need this level of production to continue. Ball’s defensive progress could prove just as important as his scoring when the Timberwolves eventually welcome their leading star back. item.description: Six Italy players at risk of quarter-final suspension if booked against Belgium Italy have a decisive final Nations League group stage match away against Belgium coming up on Sunday evening , and six of Roberto Mancini’s players will need to avoid a booking if they are to remain eligible to feature in the quarter-finals assuming that the Azzurri qualify. Italy sit at the top of their Nations League group heading into Sunday’s final round of fixtures. The Nazionale have picked up 10 points from their first five games of the competition, the same as second-placed France. Sunday’s opponents Belgium, who beat Italy 2-0 in September, are in third on nine points and Turkey will finish last given that they remain on zero points. MILAN – NOVEMBER 12: Davide Frattesi celebrates scoring his team’s second goal with teammates during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match against France at San Siro Stadium on November 12, 2026 in Milan. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) A draw against Belgium will be enough for Italy to claim a spot in the Nations League quarter-finals, but a victory is required to mathematically secure top spot without relying on results elsewhere. Italy cannot win the group if they lose against Belgium and will require Turkey to beat France if they are to lose and still qualify for the quarter-finals. Which Italy players are at risk of suspension against Belgium? Francesco Pio Esposito celebrates scoring for Italy against Luxembourg (@optapaolo) 11 different Italy players have been booked across their first five matches of the 2026-27 Nations League campaign. Six of those players are in the matchday squad to face Belgium on Sunday: Gianluigi Donnarumma, Alessandro Bastoni, Nicolo Fagioli, Antonio Vergara, Pio Esposito and Gianluca Scamacca. Davide Frattesi, Moise Kean, Daniel Maldini, Gianluca Mancini and Matteo Ruggeri have also been booked this Nations League campaign, but are not in the matchday squad to face Belgium . When do Nations League yellow cards reset? BOLOGNA – OCTOBER 05: Gianluigi Donnarumma and Alessandro Bastoni of Italy during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Italy and Türkiye at Renato Dall’Ara Stadium on October 05, 2026 in Bologna. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Players earn one-match suspensions for every even number of yellow cards they earn during the Nations League group stage and quarter-finals, i.e. after every second and fourth booking. Yellow cards will be wiped at the end of the quarter-final stage and will be reset ahead of the Nations League finals, which includes both semi-finals and the final, and is set to be held between June 9 and June 13, 2027.
